description: The plot illustrates the relationship between Initial Confidence and Accuracy, comparing three different accuracy metrics. The x-axis, labeled Initial Confidence, has a linear scale, ranging from 0.81 to 0.99 with a tick label interval of 0.01. The y-axis, labeled Accuracy, also has a linear scale, spanning from 0.0 to 1.0 with a tick label interval of 0.2. The plot displays three lines: a blue solid line representing a metric with error bars, an orange dashed line with diamond markers representing Δ Accuracy, and a green dash-dot line with square markers representing Initial Accuracy. The blue line starts at approximately 1.0 on the y-axis at x = 0.81, remains relatively steady with minor fluctuations, and ends at around 0.96 at x = 0.99. The orange Δ Accuracy line begins at about 0.4, decreases with some fluctuations to around 0.1 at x = 0.93, and further drops to approximately 0.07 at x = 0.99. The green Initial Accuracy line starts at roughly 0.5, generally increases with some fluctuations, and ends at around 0.9 at x = 0.99.
